findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as admitted
findings.description: Propagating the store error does not undo `tagDeviceUI` caching the device before its database write (lines 83–94). At capacity, a new device’s first request fails, but retrying with the same ID hits the cache and authenticates successfully for 29 minutes. Cache only successful admissions, and add a service-level test covering repeated requests from a rejected device.

findings.title: Omitting the device header bypasses enforcement
findings.description: Authentication relies exclusively on `TagDevice` returning a limit error. However, `TagDevice` returns success immediately when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is absent (`impl.go:119–122`). A client can therefore omit this client-controlled header and obtain an anonymous identity even when capacity is exhausted. Define and enforce an admission policy for unidentified requests, with authentication-level coverage.

findings.title: Concurrent admissions can exceed the configured limit
findings.description: The count and subsequent insert use separate database sessions without atomic admission control. With one slot remaining, concurrent requests for different device IDs can both observe available capacity and insert successfully. Serialize admission through a database-safe mechanism that also works across Grafana instances, and test concurrent admissions at the boundary.
